statement:
On a table there are 2013 cards, each with a different integer from 1 to 2013 written on it, all face down (so the numbers are not visible). One may select any set of cards and ask whether the average of the numbers on those cards is an integer; the answer will be truthful.

a) Find all numbers that can be determined with certainty by a sequence of such questions.

b) We want to divide the cards into groups such that the contents of each group are known (even though individual card values within the group are not). What is the maximum number of groups that can be obtained?

In a convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\), angles \(\angle A\) and \(\angle C\) are equal, and the bisector of \(\angle B\) passes through the midpoint of side \(CD\). If \(CD = 3\,AD\), calculate \(\dfrac{AB}{BC}\).

Find how many 2013-digit numbers \(d_1 d_2 \cdots d_{2013}\) with all digits odd satisfy: the sum of 1809 terms
\[d_1 \cdot d_2 + d_2 \cdot d_3 + \cdots + d_{1809} \cdot d_{1810}\]
has remainder 1 when divided by 4, and the sum of 203 terms
\[d_{1810} \cdot d_{1811} + d_{1811} \cdot d_{1812} + \cdots + d_{2012} \cdot d_{2013}\]
also has remainder 1 when divided by 4.
Let \(x \geq 5\), \(y \geq 6\), \(z \geq 7\) satisfy \(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \geq 125\). Find the minimum value of \(x + y + z\).

The integers from 1 to 2013 are written on a blackboard. The allowed operation is to choose a positive integer \(a\) and replace every number \(b \geq a\) on the board by \(b - a\) (in particular, every occurrence of \(a\) becomes 0). After several operations, the numbers on the board have a sum equal to 10. Determine all possible multisets of numbers that can remain on the board.

A positive integer \(n\) is called pretty if there exist two divisors \(d_1, d_2\) of \(n\) (\(1 \leq d_1, d_2 \leq n\)) such that \(d_2 - d_1 = d\) for each divisor \(d\) of \(n\) with \(1 < d < n\). Find the smallest pretty number larger than 401 that is a multiple of 401.
